issues.legal_issue: A claimant may receive the additional compensation benefit when the Reference Court makes its award after the benefit takes effect, even if the Collector made an earlier award.
material_facts: The land was acquired under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and the Collector made the compensation award before the 1984 amendments took effect.
The landowners sought a reference under Section 18, and the Reference Court made its award after the amendments took effect.
The Reference Court granted the additional benefit, and the High Court upheld that grant.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were entitled to the additional amount under Section 23(1-A), and the appeals challenging that entitlement were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(1-A) confers a substantive right and places a duty on the Court deciding the reference to award the additional amount. Substantive provisions ordinarily operate prospectively unless the statutory language and context show retrospective intent. The term “Court” refers to the court defined by Section 3(d), which decides a reference under Section 18; it cannot be read as “Collector.” The Court rejected the narrower interpretation in Union of India v. Filip Tiago De Gama and distinguished the issues addressed in Union of India v. Raghuvir Singh; it referred to K. Kamala Jammannia-varu and Bhag Singh in discussing the statutory scheme.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_reference: A landowner whose land was acquired sought a court determination of compensation through a reference proceeding.
predicates.reference_court_award_after_benefit_take: The court deciding the compensation reference made its award after the additional-benefit provision took effect.
predicates.collector_award_before_transitional_cuto: The Collector had made the initial compensation award before the statutory transitional cutoff.

issues.definition: When a compensation reference results in a court award after the benefit takes effect, the claimant is entitled to the additional compensation even if the Collector had awarded compensation earlier.

issues.legal_issue: The transitional provision extends the additional compensation benefit to covered acquisition proceedings even where the reference court had already made its award before the benefit took effect.
material_facts: The Court construed Section 30(1)(a) together with Section 23(1-A).

It considered acquisition proceedings that were pending on the transitional cutoff date and in which the Collector had not yet made an award, including proceedings in which the court had already made an award before the new provision took effect.
issues.conclusion: In those covered proceedings, the additional amount is payable even if the court made its award before the new provision took effect.
issues.legal_principle: Section 30(1)(a) of the Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1984 makes Section 23(1-A) applicable to acquisition proceedings pending on the specified transitional date where the Collector had not made an award by then. Read with the word “also” in Section 30(1) and the plain language of Section 23(1-A), the transitional provision does not exclude a proceeding merely because the court had already made its award. The Court disapproved the contrary narrow approaches in Union of India v. Filip Tiago De Gama and Jaiwant Laxman P. Sardesai, and noted approval of State of Punjab v. Krishan Lal and Maya Devi v. Union Territory of Chandigarh.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The matter concerns acquisition of land and determination of compensation under the acquisition law.
predicates.proceeding_pending_at_transitional_cutof: The acquisition proceeding remained pending on the statutory transitional cutoff date.
predicates.collector_had_not_awarded_by_cutoff: The Collector had not made an award by that cutoff date.

issues.definition: If an acquisition proceeding was pending at the transitional cutoff and the Collector had not yet awarded compensation, the claimant is entitled to the additional compensation, even if the court had already awarded compensation.

issues.legal_issue: A pending appeal does not make the additional compensation benefit available when both the Collector and the Reference Court made their awards before the benefit took effect.
material_facts: The Court distinguished a proceeding still awaiting a reference-court award from a case in which the Collector and the Reference Court had both already made awards and only an appeal remained pending.
It treated an appellate court’s decision as a decree rather than a new award for purposes of Section 23(1-A).
issues.conclusion: The additional benefit does not apply merely because an appeal remains pending after both the Collector and the Reference Court have made their awards.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(1-A) speaks of an “award,” which is distinct from a “decree.” Under Section 3(d), the relevant Court is the principal court of original jurisdiction, including the court deciding a Section 18 reference. When both awards predate the provision, an appellate court deciding an appeal makes a decree, not an award that brings Section 23(1-A) into operation. The Court’s construction is consistent with its discussion of Union of India v. Raghuvir Singh and its reliance on K. Kamala Jammannia-varu rather than the expanded reading in Bhag Singh.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: A party is pursuing an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.collector_award_before_benefit_takes_eff: The Collector made the initial compensation award before the additional-benefit provision took effect.
predicates.reference_court_award_before_benefit_tak: The court deciding the compensation reference also made its award before the additional-benefit provision took effect.

issues.definition: When both the Collector and the reference court have made their awards before the benefit takes effect, a pending compensation appeal alone does not entitle the claimant to the additional compensation.
